Subject: MAP / Eval plan - quick validation of cost assumptions for HelixMed

Hi Jared —

Thanks again for the time on Thursday. I pulled together an initial mutual action plan and a short eval scope we think aligns with HelixMed's goals (data privacy + fast clinical inference). Before I lock timelines we want to validate a couple of unit-econ assumptions so the MAP has realistic milestones and procurement asks. Two quick asks: 

1) Can you confirm expected average input+output token sizes per API call for your main use-case (triage summarization)? Even a ballpark (e.g., 600 -> 100 tokens) helps.
2) Is your procurement team ok evaluating a 30-day pilot on our Hosted tier, or do you need Dedicated from day one? If Dedicated, who should I loop in on capacity sizing?

I'm attaching a draft MAP + evaluation plan with line-items labeled "cost checks". The three things we'd like to validate in the MAP: tokens/$ for the candidate model, caching assumptions (how many queries are repeated), and realistic batching targets during peak window.

I'll follow up with a simple worked example in case it's useful. Call/zoom fine if you prefer.

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0123

- What batching sizes do you usually see for low-latency interactive workloads? We can't tolerate much tail latency.

Procurement contact is S. Procure (s.procure@helixmed.com) — feel free to loop them if you need legal/PO info.

Subject: Fw: MAP / Eval plan - quick validation of cost assumptions for HelixMed

Ava / Rishi —

Forwarding Jared's numbers. He gave token sizes and prefers Hosted for the eval. I've sketched a quick worked example in the MAP spreadsheet (tab: "cost_worked_example") showing two model choices: Redwood-7B-fp16 and Redwood-7B-q4 (quantized). 

Key assumptions I used (we can update):
- avg total tokens per call = 890 (750 in + 140 out)
- baseline throughput target = 30 rps at peak (Helix said their busiest clinic hours)
- batching window: 25 ms initial, target batch size 6-10 during steady state batching
- prefix caching: assume 15% of calls share cached context on day 1, 28% by week 4 as templates stabilize

Prelim numbers in the sheet:
- Redwood-7B-fp16 (hosted): $0.0009 per token => ~$0.80 per 1k tokens; effective tokens/$ (no cache) ~1,111 tokens per $1; with 20% cache hit -> effective tokens/$ ~1,389 tokens per $1
- Redwood-7B-q4 (hosted, quantized): approx 18% lower runtime cost in our experiments; factor that into the sheet for an apples-to-apples compare

I'll mark cells with assumptions anchored to our telemetry so legal/procurement have a conservative starting point. Rishi — can you review SLA / latency tolerances and propose whether we should suggest a Dedicated pilot instead? Connor, can you add an item listing the exact telemetry we will provide during eval (token-level cost, latency P50/P95/P99, cache-hit ratio)?

- Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Hansen <jhansen@helixmed.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, S. Procure <s.procure@helixmed.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP / Eval plan - quick validation of cost assumptions for HelixMed

Jared —

Thanks for the numbers; good baseline. Quick worked example below (we'll add the table into the MAP spreadsheet so procurement has a single page to review):

Worked example (hosted eval, Redwood-7B-q4 recommended):
- Avg tokens/call: 890
- Calls/day (pilot): 120k daytime triage calls (pilot window estimate) -> daily tokens = 106.8M
- Baseline hosted unit price: $0.00085 per token (quantized runtime advantage factored)
- Raw daily cost (no cache) = 106.8M * $0.00085 = $90,780/day (pilot) -> that figure assumes no batching/caching savings

Conservative discounts/savings to propose in MAP:
- Batching: realistic steady-state batching at peak -> 10-15% token-processing efficiency gain (because kernel reuse and request coalescing), we model 12% here
- Caching: we model a 20% cache-hit for prefixed templates during the pilot ramp, which reduces billed tokens accordingly

Applying savings: 90,780 * (1 - 0.12 - 0.20) = $56,560/day (modeled pilot cost)

Notes / guidance:
- Those are conservative (we don't double-count improvements; batching reduces compute but not billed tokens for output — our billing unit is tokens generated + consumed; server-side savings can be presented as lower vendor cost and used to justify a hybrid price during evaluation)
- For procurement: propose a 30-day hosted eval cap of $75K with telemetry and a reconciliation clause. If Helix wants Dedicated for first-run, we'll run a quick capacity-sizing call (needs GPU estate + model pinning discussion).

Action items:
- Ava: share the capped eval proposal with Procurement (S. Procure) and confirm PO cadence.
- Connor: add the telemetry dashboard link to the MAP (P50/P95/P99 latency, tokens per request, cache-hit).
- Marissa: update MAP spreadsheet to include a "reconciliation" row explaining how batching/caching were estimated and a fallback price.

Happy to take a 20-min call tomorrow to walk the procurement team through the worked example.

- Rishi
